slides.heading: Changing Variable Values
slides.body: Changing Variable Values is part of Variables and Primitive Data Types. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Changing Variable Values
slides.body: A variable can be assigned a new value. When this happens, the old value is replaced by the new value.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Changing a variable is like updating a whiteboard. The new information replaces what was written before.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use clear variable names and match the data type to the kind of value you need to store.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Create a variable named level, change it to a new value, then print it.
slides.hint: Assign level again using a new value before printing.

quiz.prompt_text: What happens when you assign a new value to an existing variable in Python?

options: Python creates a second variable with the same name
Python keeps both old and new values
Python replaces the old value with the new value
Python causes an error because variables cannot change

quiz.explanation: Right! Reassigning a variable replaces the old value entirely — like erasing a whiteboard and writing something new.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines in the correct order to set points to 10, update it to 15, and print the final value.
quiz.explanation: points starts at 10, then is reassigned to 15 which replaces the original, and finally print() shows the current value of 15.

quiz.prompt_text: Create a variable named level set to 1, change it to 2, and print the updated value.

content.hint: Assign level a new value on the next line, then use print(level).

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: Write level = 2 after the first assignment. print(level) then outputs 2. Reassigning updates the stored value completely.
